key_insight: Enforcing linear completeness in PIML removes a key obstacle to mesh-refinement convergence and enables rigorous H1- and L2-norm error estimates.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient substructure-based finite element analysis by learning reusable numerical shape functions while preserving finite element conformity.
method: Bound PIML error using finite element discretization error and network generalization error.
Identify a learning-induced error term that need not decrease under mesh refinement when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced.
Reconstruct transition-matrix columns using linear displacement constraints so the numerical shape-function space contains linear polynomials.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments reported in the abstract verify the theory and demonstrate optimal convergence rates, good generalization, and numerical stability.
watch_item: Linear completeness requires explicit constraint enforcement, and total error still depends on network generalization; the abstract does not quantify performance on unseen geometries or materials.
paper_title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
